subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 28-year-old woman presents for preconception counseling. Her first child was born with a myelomeningocele and required surgical closure on the first day of life. She has no chronic illnesses, takes no regular medications, and her diet is generally balanced. She now plans to conceive within the next few months and wants to know how to reduce the risk of a neural tube defect in this pregnancy.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate recommendation?

options.text: Begin folic acid supplementation at 20 weeks of gestation
Begin folic acid supplementation as soon as the pregnancy test is positive
Begin folic acid supplementation at least 1 month before conception and continue through pregnancy
Begin folic acid supplementation immediately after delivery
Supplement folic acid only if plasma homocysteine becomes elevated during pregnancy

explanation_correct: The neural tube closes within the first 4 weeks of gestation, often before a woman knows she is pregnant, so folic acid must be started at least 1 month before conception and continued through pregnancy. Folate is converted to tetrahydrofolic acid, a coenzyme for one-carbon transfer reactions required for synthesis of the nitrogenous bases of DNA and RNA. Adequate periconceptional folate reduces the risk of neural tube defects such as spina bifida and anencephaly.

explanation_incorrect.A: Starting at 20 weeks is far too late, because neural tube closure is complete by about 4 weeks of gestation.
explanation_incorrect.B: Waiting for a positive pregnancy test frequently misses the period of neural tube closure, which occurs before most women know they are pregnant.
explanation_incorrect.D: Supplementation after delivery cannot prevent a defect in a pregnancy that has already been completed.
explanation_incorrect.E: Supplementation is recommended for all women planning pregnancy, not only those with an elevated homocysteine level.

educationalObjective: Folic acid must be started at least 1 month before conception and continued during pregnancy to reduce the risk of neural tube defects.
